item.title: Gas Markets Spike on Ras Laffan Disruption — TTF Surges 32% Overnight
item.description: Day 21 of the Iran-Israel war brought the unthinkable — Iranian missiles struck Ras Laffan, crippling 20% of global LNG supply and sending TTF surging 32% overnight to €82.5/MWh. With EU storage at 28.5% and the Russian LNG ban 12 days away, the refill math is now structurally broken without a ceasefire. The Council validated 12 of 20 trade ideas, eliminating 8 duplicates and contradictions; the TTF Sum-26/Win-26 spread and Win-26 outright long remain highest conviction.

item.title: TTF Slips Below €50 as HH Decouples — JKM Surges Past $19 on Qatar Retaliation
item.description: Day 20 changed the character of this war — from transit blockade to production destruction. Israel struck South Pars, Iran retaliated against Qatar and Saudi facilities, and Trump threatens Kharg Island. With EU storage at 28.9% and the March 19 summit opening today, the refill math is broken regardless of geopolitics. The council validated 11 of 17 trade ideas, eliminating 6 duplicates and incomplete structures; the Win/Sum spread and JKM-TTF widener remain highest conviction.

item.title: TTF Steadies at €50.75 as Hormuz Selective Passage Regime Takes Shape — HH Slips to $3.13 on Shoulder Season
item.description: Iran's two-tier Hormuz — open for friends, closed for the West — is the new structural reality, and the EU summit on March 19 will test whether Brussels blinks on ETS and the LNG ban. With storage at 29% and 70 bcm to inject before November, the refill math doesn't forgive diplomatic hesitation. The council validated 13 of 21 trade ideas, culling 8 redundancies and contradictions; the TTF Win-26 long and the €50 straddle remain highest conviction.

item.title: Mild Temps Cool HH to $3.13 While TTF Holds €50 — JKM Retreats on Easing Hormuz Fears
item.description: Iran's 'safe passage' overture is the first diplomatic crack since Hormuz Day 1 — but with EU storage at 29.1% and the April LNG ban 40 days away, the supply math doesn't care about diplomacy. The council validated 13 of 21 trade ideas, culling 8 duplicates and vague structures; the TTF Win-26 long and the straddle remain highest conviction, while the ceasefire put spread is essential insurance against the snap-back no one expects.

item.title: Mojtaba Effect: TTF Holds €50 as New Iran Leader Kills Reopening Hopes — HH Gains on Late-Season Cold
item.description: Mojtaba Khamenei's first act as Supreme Leader — vowing Hormuz stays shut indefinitely — removes the last near-term ceasefire catalyst. TTF holds €50 as the market prices duration, not resolution. The council validated 16 of 21 trade ideas, culling 5 duplicates and contradictions; the JKM-TTF widener and TTF Win-26 long remain highest conviction, while the €50 straddle captures the binary Hormuz outcome.

item.title: TTF au-dessus de €49 — La guerre iranienne maintient la prime de risque
item.description: Hormuz Day 12. TTF holds above 49 EUR, EU storage at 29 pct. The market is pricing duration, not resolution. Trade the refill squeeze.

item.title: Post-Crash Whiplash: TTF Reclaims €50 as IRGC Kills Ceasefire Euphoria
item.description: Post-crash whiplash defines the session: TTF touched €46.70 on ceasefire hopes before IRGC's blockade vow triggered a 5% reversal to €49.85. The council validated 11 trades from 21, culling 10 doublons and contradictions — the TTF Apr €48/€55 call spread (unanimous) and Win-26 outright long remain highest conviction, while the €50 straddle captures the binary Hormuz outcome.
